record.original_question: What composition and energy spectrum of cosmic antinuclei should be predicted for antimatter objects in the Galaxy in order to confront AMS02 searches, when propagation through Galactic magnetic fields and inelastic processes during propagation are included?

evidence.quote: In any case to confront AMS02 searches the prediction for composition and spectrum of cosmic antinuclei from antimatter objects in our Galaxy should be made. Such prediction inevitably involves the account for propagation of antinuclei in galactic magnetic fields [50] as well as for the inelastic processes in such propagation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a hypothetical scenario in which the Milky Way contains compact astrophysical objects made of antimatter (antistars or antimatter clouds) that emit cosmic antinuclei (antiprotons, antideuterons, antihelium, and possibly heavier antinuclei) at their sources. Assume each antimatter source emits antinuclei with an injection composition and rigidity spectrum analogous to those produced by ordinary stellar/cosmic-ray sources of matter. The emitted antinuclei then propagate through the Galaxy, undergoing diffusion and convection in the Galactic magnetic field, energy losses (ionization, Coulomb, adiabatic, synchrotron, inverse Compton), reacceleration, and inelastic interactions (annihilation and inelastic non-annihilating collisions) with interstellar gas, modeled by a transport equation of the form
  ∂N/∂t = ∇·(D ∇N − V N) + ∂/∂p[ p² D_pp ∂/∂p (N/p²) ] − ∂/∂p[ ṗ N − (p/3)(∇·V) N ] − (1/τ_f + 1/τ_r) N + Q,
together with solar-modulation at the heliospheric boundary.

Problem: Determine, for each antinuclear species A (with A = p̄, d̄, ³He̅, ⁴He̅, …), the predicted composition ratios N_A/N_p̄ and the differential top-of-atmosphere kinetic-energy spectra dΦ_A/dE_k(E_k) at Earth, as functions of the source distribution of antimatter objects in the Galaxy, of the injection spectrum, and of the propagation parameters (D₀, δ, halo height L, Alfvén velocity, convection velocity, and inelastic cross sections), in a form suitable for direct comparison with AMS-02 search sensitivities over the kinetic energy range 0.1–100 GeV/nucleon.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (e.g. arXiv:2404.13114, arXiv:2505.04692) compute cosmic antinuclei spectra under various source assumptions (dark matter, primordial black holes, secondary production) using state-of-the-art Galactic propagation models constrained by AMS-02 antiproton and light-nuclei data. However, no consensus prediction for the composition and spectrum of antinuclei from antimatter objects in the Galaxy that fully accounts for magnetic-field propagation and inelastic processes has been established, and the AMS-02 antihelium candidate events remain unexplained. The problem is therefore active and open.

status_evidence.title: Cosmic-Ray Propagation Models Elucidate the Prospects for Antinuclei Detection
status_evidence.snippet: State-of-the-art cosmic-ray propagation models, fit to high-precision antiproton and cosmic-ray nuclei (B, Be, Li) data, constrain the antinuclei flux from both astrophysical and dark matter annihilation models.
status_evidence.claim: Active research area; predictions still depend strongly on propagation model choice.

status_evidence.title: Antinuclei from Primordial Black Holes
status_evidence.snippet: Recent studies use state-of-the-art models for Galactic propagation, relevant for a realistic evaluation of the detectable spectra of CR antinuclei.
status_evidence.claim: Predictions of antinuclei spectra including propagation are an ongoing research effort.

status_evidence.title: Cosmic-ray Antinuclei as Messengers of New Physics: Status and Outlook for the New Decade
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews status and outlook for antinuclei searches, noting outstanding theoretical and modeling challenges.
status_evidence.claim: Composition/spectrum predictions confronting AMS-02 remain open.
